items.monitorsDescription: Проверяйте сайты, API и серверы и узнавайте, когда они перестают работать.
items.slosDescription: Цели надёжности и сколько бюджета ошибок ещё осталось.
items.storageArraysDescription: Monitor storage arrays such as Pure Storage FlashArray and FlashBlade.
items.statusPagesDescription: Показывайте клиентам, что работает, а что нет.
items.incidentsDescription: Проблемы, которые затрагивают ваших пользователей, — реагируйте и устраняйте.
items.alertsDescription: Проблемы, которые команде стоит проверить, пока их не заметили пользователи.
items.onCallDutyDescription: Кого вызывают и кто следующий, если никто не ответил.
items.sentinelInsightsDescription: Proactive findings from OneUptime AI's telemetry watch — new exceptions, spikes, latency regressions and metric drift.
items.securityEventsDescription: SIEM signals correlated with your observability data.
items.metricsDescription: Отслеживайте и визуализируйте системные метрики ваших сервисов.
items.tracesDescription: Отслеживайте запросы по всем вашим сервисам.
items.performanceProfilesDescription: Найдите медленные функции и горячие точки памяти.
items.exceptionsDescription: Отслеживайте и устраняйте баги во всех ваших сервисах.
items.llmObservabilityDescription: Наблюдайте за вызовами LLM и ИИ-агентов — токены, стоимость, задержка, промпты и ответы.
items.iotDescription: Monitor IoT device fleets — battery, connectivity, temperature and availability.
items.inventoryDescription: Всё, что OneUptime знает о вашей инфраструктуре, в одном списке.
items.topologyDescription: Посмотрите, как связаны ваши сервисы и инфраструктура.
items.servicesDescription: Каталогизируйте каждый сервис, который вы запускаете.
items.databasesDescription: Все базы данных, к которым обращаются ваши приложения, с метриками движка.
items.queuesDescription: Очереди сообщений и топики из ваших трассировок и брокеров.
items.dockerSwarmDescription: Monitor Docker Swarm clusters, nodes, services and tasks.
items.networkDescription: Monitor network devices via SNMP and group them into sites.
items.proxmoxDescription: Мониторинг кластеров, узлов и гостевых систем Proxmox.
items.vmwareDescription: Мониторинг vCenter, хостов ESXi, виртуальных машин и хранилищ данных.
items.cephDescription: Мониторинг кластеров, OSD и пулов Ceph.
items.hostsDescription: Отслеживайте состояние серверов и виртуальных машин по всему парку.
items.serverlessDescription: Мониторинг бессерверных / FaaS-функций, таких как AWS Lambda и Cloud Functions.
items.cloudDescription: Мониторинг управляемых облачных вычислений и ресурсов IaaS/PaaS в AWS, Azure и Google Cloud.
items.rumDescription: Мониторинг браузерных и мобильных приложений с помощью OpenTelemetry RUM.
items.dashboardsDescription: Стройте графики по метрикам, логам и трассировкам.
items.workflowsDescription: Автоматизации без кода, например сообщение в Slack при открытии инцидента.
items.runbooksDescription: Многократно используемые процедуры реагирования: ручные чек-листы или скрипты.
items.formsDescription: Формы, которые может заполнить любой, создающие инциденты или плановые обслуживания.
items.aiChatDescription: Chat with AI — it answers from your logs, traces, metrics, incidents, alerts and monitors, and cites every query.
items.teamsDescription: Объединяйте пользователей в команды и назначайте разрешения.
items.projectSettingsDescription: Оплата, API-ключи, SSO, метки и настройки уведомлений.
items.codeDescription: Попросите ИИ изменить ваш код и открыть Pull Request. Подключите GitHub здесь.
items.dataSecurityDescription: Находите конфиденциальные данные в облаках, базах данных и телеметрии, смотрите, у кого есть к ним доступ, и в первую очередь исправляйте самое важное.

Title: Заголовок
Notify subscribers that this incident wa: Уведомить подписчиков о создании этого инцидента
Subscribers were not told about this inc: Подписчики не были уведомлены об этом инциденте, так как он был скрыт со страниц состояния. Отметьте этот пункт, чтобы отправить им уведомление о создании инцидента сейчас. Для решённых инцидентов он по умолчанию снят, чтобы публикация старого инцидента для истории не объявляла его новым.
Send subscribers the edited announcement: Отправляет подписчикам отредактированное объявление с пометкой об обновлении. Не отмечайте для мелких исправлений, например опечаток.

Subscribers will receive the edited note: Подписчики получат отредактированную заметку с пометкой об обновлении.

Your own HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, rend: Ваш собственный HTML, CSS и JavaScript, отображаемый в песочнице.
AI will analyze this exception, identify: AI will analyze this exception, identify the root cause, and submit a Pull Request with the fix to your code repository.
Add Monitoring Criteria for this monitor: Добавьте критерии мониторинга для этого монитора. Отслеживайте различные свойства.
Alert metrics for this monitor - count,: Метрики оповещений для этого монитора — количество, время подтверждения, время разрешения и продолжительность.
All on-call policies you are currently o: Все политики дежурств, по которым вы сейчас на дежурстве во всех ваших проектах.

The current token stops working, and emb: Текущий токен перестанет работать, а встроенные значки не будут работать, пока вы не обновите их новым токеном.
Are you sure you want to remove this SLA: Вы уверены, что хотите удалить это правило SLA из инцидента? Это удалит все данные отслеживания SLA для этого правила.
Assigns pods to nodes based on resource: Назначает поды на узлы на основе требований к ресурсам, аффинитетов и ограничений. Отслеживает пропускную способность планирования, давление очереди и активность вытеснения.
Automatically combine related alerts int: Автоматически объединяйте связанные оповещения в логические контейнеры, называемые эпизодами
Automatically combine related incidents: Автоматически объединяйте связанные инциденты в логические контейнеры, называемые эпизодами

CPU and memory usage for pods in this st: Использование ЦП и памяти подами в этом StatefulSet за последние 6 часов.
CPU and memory usage for this container: Использование ЦП и памяти этим контейнером за последние 6 часов.
Использование ЦП и памяти этим контейнером.
CPU, memory, and container-level resourc: Использование ЦП, памяти и ресурсов на уровне контейнера для этого пода за последние 6 часов.
CPU, memory, filesystem, and network usa: Использование ЦП, памяти, файловой системы и сети для этого узла за последние 6 часов.
Central management entity that validates: Центральная сущность управления, которая проверяет и обслуживает все REST-операции. Отслеживает пропускную способность запросов, задержку, частоту ошибок и состояние подключений.
Choose which Twilio account to use for t: Выберите, какую учётную запись Twilio использовать для этой политики входящих вызовов
Cilium agent managing security identitie: Агент Cilium, управляющий идентичностями безопасности, сетевыми политиками, BPF-картами и IPAM. Отслеживает состояние политик, распределение идентичностей и ошибки агента.
Cluster DNS server handling all in-clust: DNS-сервер кластера, обрабатывающий все запросы разрешения имён внутри кластера. Отслеживает пропускную способность запросов, задержку, эффективность кэша, пересылку и ошибки.

Distributed key-value store backing all: Распределённое хранилище ключ-значение, поддерживающее всё состояние кластера. Отслеживает размер базы данных, задержку дискового ввода-вывода, стабильность лидера и состояние репликации.

Эпизоды следуют тому же прогрессу состояний, что и инциденты

HTTP and TCP traffic flowing through Env: HTTP- и TCP-трафик, проходящий через прокси-сайдкары Envoy. Охватывает пропускную способность запросов, задержку, размеры полезной нагрузки и жизненный цикл соединений.

Вот история доступности этого монитора за 90 дней.

How calls are routed through your escala: Как вызовы маршрутизируются через ваши правила эскалации
How on-call policies work with alerts an: Как политики дежурств работают с оповещениями и эпизодами
How on-call policies work with incidents: Как политики дежурств работают с инцидентами и эпизодами

How to set up on-call policies for incid: Как настроить политики дежурств для группировки инцидентов
Слой наблюдаемости сетевых потоков Hubble. Отслеживает пропускную способность обработки потоков, видимость DNS, флаги TCP-соединений и отброшенные потоки.

Istio Pilot manages xDS configuration di: Istio Pilot управляет распределением конфигурации xDS по всем прокси Envoy. Отслеживает пропускную способность отправки, ошибки, время конвергенции и конфликты слушателей.

Kubernetes events for this cronjob in th: События Kubernetes для этого CronJob за последние 24 часа.

LLM Providers help you automate and enha: Поставщики LLM помогают автоматизировать и улучшить ваш рабочий процесс управления инцидентами с помощью функций на базе ИИ.
Linkerd control plane components: identi: Компоненты плоскости управления Linkerd: identity (выпуск сертификатов mTLS), destination (обнаружение сервисов) и proxy injector (внедрение сайдкара).
Live CPU, memory, network, and process m: Метрики ЦП, памяти, сети и процессов в реальном времени, агрегированные по каждому контейнеру на этом хосте. Используйте селектор временного диапазона для увеличения или уменьшения.
Live OpenTelemetry logs from all contain: Логи OpenTelemetry в реальном времени от всех контейнеров на этом хосте Docker. Используйте панель фильтров для фильтрации по уровню серьёзности, trace id или любому атрибуту ресурса.
Logs for this container from the last 6: Логи этого контейнера за последние 6 часов.
Low-level Envoy sidecar proxy metrics. T: Низкоуровневые метрики прокси-сайдкара Envoy. Отслеживает пулы upstream-соединений, тайм-ауты запросов, повторные попытки и сбои соединений.
Metric data from around when this incide: Данные метрик примерно в момент объявления этого инцидента.
Network proxy on each node maintaining i: Сетевой прокси на каждом узле, поддерживающий правила iptables/IPVS для маршрутизации Service. Отслеживает задержку синхронизации правил, время сетевого программирования и события изменений.
No custom metrics have been captured yet: Пользовательские метрики ещё не захвачены. Используйте oneuptime.captureMetric() в скрипте монитора, чтобы захватить пользовательские метрики.
Packet forwarding, drops, and policy enf: Пересылка пакетов, отбрасывания и применение политик на уровне eBPF datapath. Охватывает пропускную способность, управление конечными точками и регенерацию BPF-программ.
Please check this if you do not want to: Установите этот флажок, если не хотите следовать переадресациям.
Please select an SSO provider to log in: Выберите поставщика SSO для входа в этот проект.
Pods with the highest resource utilizati: Поды с наибольшим потреблением ресурсов в этом кластере.
Preview the live badge rendering using t: Предварительный просмотр рендеринга значка с использованием текущего токена безопасности.
Real-time SLA status and deadlines for t: Статус SLA и сроки в реальном времени для этого инцидента. Таймеры обновляются автоматически.
Request headers, body, and redirect sett: Заголовки запроса, тело и настройки переадресации
Request throughput, response latency, an: Метрики пропускной способности запросов, задержки ответов и TCP-соединений от прокси-сайдкаров Linkerd.
Reserve a phone number from Twilio to re: Зарезервируйте номер телефона из Twilio для получения входящих вызовов
Retry settings and more: Настройки повторных попыток и многое другое
Review and copy the token required to ac: Просмотрите и скопируйте токен, необходимый для доступа к встроенному значку. Сохраняйте его в тайне, чтобы предотвратить несанкционированный доступ.
Review the rendered documentation before: Просмотрите отрендеренную документацию перед тем, как поделиться ею с командой.
Runs core control loops that reconcile c: Выполняет основные циклы управления, которые согласовывают состояние кластера. Отслеживает глубину очереди работ, задержку обработки, повторные попытки и пропускную способность по всем контроллерам.
Search for phone numbers available in yo: Поиск номеров телефонов, доступных в вашей учётной записи Twilio. Номер будет зарезервирован с использованием вашего баланса Twilio.
Settings to prevent rapid state changes: Настройки для предотвращения быстрых изменений состояния и шума оповещений
Настройки для предотвращения быстрых изменений состояния и шума инцидентов
Specific pods and nodes that are driving: Конкретные поды и узлы, влияющие на текущее состояние. Нажмите для расследования.
The specific resource (e.g. host, pod, c: Конкретный ресурс (например, хост, под, контейнер), который вызвал это оповещение. Присутствует, когда монитор метрик группируется по одному или нескольким атрибутам.
Конкретный ресурс (например, хост, под, контейнер), который вызвал этот инцидент. Присутствует, когда монитор метрик группируется по одному или нескольким атрибутам.
Unarchive this exception. You will be no: Извлечь это исключение из архива. Вы будете получать уведомления при возникновении этого исключения.
Use an existing Twilio phone number or r: Используйте существующий номер телефона Twilio или зарезервируйте новый

Enable this to add a grace period before: Включите это, чтобы добавить льготный период перед автоматическим устранением эпизода после устранения всех его оповещений. Без этого эпизод устранялся бы сразу после устранения оповещений, а затем мог бы повторно открыться через мгновение, если проблема возникнет снова.

Без этого эпизод устранялся бы сразу после устранения инцидентов, а затем мог бы повторно открыться через мгновение, если проблема возникнет снова.

Без этого эпизоды оставались бы открытыми бесконечно, пока не будут устранены вручную.

Это полезно для повторяющихся проблем — если проблема возвращается вскоре после устранения, разумнее продолжать отслеживать её в том же эпизоде, а не дробить историю инцидента на несколько эпизодов.

Если отключено, все оповещения, соответствующие критериям группировки (серьёзность, заголовок, монитор и т. д.), будут объединены в один продолжающийся эпизод независимо от времени их возникновения. Если включено, оповещения группируются только при поступлении в течение указанного временного окна с момента последнего оповещения.

Grace period after all alerts resolve be: Льготный период после устранения всех оповещений перед автоматическим устранением эпизода. Помогает предотвратить ненужные изменения состояния при «мерцании» оповещений — когда оповещения быстро переключаются между сработавшим и устранённым состояниями.

Put related alerts into one episode, so: Объединяйте связанные оповещения в один эпизод, чтобы команда работала над одной проблемой, а не над потоком оповещений. Правила проверяются сверху вниз, и срабатывает первое подходящее - перетащите правило, чтобы изменить его место.

Как только лицензия будет активирована, запросы SCIM снова будут приниматься, поэтому, если токен утёк, замените его сейчас с помощью «Сбросить Bearer-токен», а затем передайте новый токен вашему поставщику удостоверений.

Monitor websites, APIs, servers and more: Следите за сайтами, API, серверами и многим другим — получайте уведомление, как только что-то перестанет работать.

An incident is a problem that affects yo: Инцидент — это проблема, которая затрагивает ваших пользователей, например сбой или замедление. Объявите инцидент, чтобы вызвать дежурного, следить за исправлением и обновить страницу статуса.

A chunk sent as the page went away was o: Фрагмент, отправленный при закрытии страницы, превысил квоту keepalive браузера. При sealed: true в подробностях это был последний фрагмент: его события отброшены, поэтому последних секунд перед закрытием страницы нет, а вместо него сеанс закрыл пустой последний фрагмент, так что сеанс всё равно завершается вместе с вкладкой, не дожидаясь тайм-аута бездействия. При sealed: false это был не последний фрагмент: он отброшен целиком, ничего не закрыто, и сеанс остаётся открытым с пробелом на месте фрагмента.

Battery charge from each device's most r: Battery charge from each device's most recent report, shown in red at 20% or below. It is the last value sent, even if the device has since stopped reporting.
Battery charge from this device's most r: Battery charge from this device's most recent report. If the device has stopped reporting, this is the last value it sent, so compare it with Last Seen.
Bytes per second clients read from and w: Bytes per second clients read from and wrote to the cluster, added up across all pools. Worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running per-pool byte counters.
Bytes per second read from and written t: Bytes per second read from and written to this pool, worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running byte counters.
Bytes per second received (In) and sent: Bytes per second received (In) and sent (Out) in each interval, added up across all nodes and network interfaces. Worked out from the running byte counters the nodes report.

Bytes per second received (In) and sent (Out), added up across every network interface the host reports, including loopback when the collector sends it. Worked out from the change in each interface's byte counters between intervals.
Bytes per second received and transmitte: Bytes per second received and transmitted in each interval, added up across every node and network interface the agent reports. Worked out from the nodes' running byte counters rather than sampled directly.
Bytes per second received plus sent, add: Bytes per second received plus sent, added up across every node and network interface and averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). The line below splits it into in and out.
Bytes per second this node received and: Bytes per second this node received and sent, added up across its network interfaces. Worked out from how much the node's network byte counters grew between points in the selected time range.
CPU Ready is the share of time a VM was: CPU Ready is the share of time a VM was ready to run but had to wait for a physical CPU. Averaged across powered-on VMs over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data), with the busiest VM below; amber from 5%, red from 10%.
CPU Ready over the selected range: Avg i: CPU Ready over the selected range: Avg is the average across powered-on VMs and Max the highest single VM in each interval. It is the share of time VMs waited for a physical CPU; above 10% they are noticeably slowed.
CPU capacity available to run VMs (effec: CPU capacity available to run VMs (effective) against the cluster's total CPU capacity, in MHz or GHz, from the latest report. Hosts in maintenance mode or not responding are left out of effective.
CPU capacity the cluster can use to run: CPU capacity the cluster can use to run VMs, out of its total CPU capacity, in MHz or GHz, from its latest report. Hosts in maintenance mode or not responding do not count toward the effective figure.
CPU in use across all ESXi hosts in each: CPU in use across all ESXi hosts in each interval of the selected range, as a share of their combined CPU capacity. Hosts with more CPU count for more.
CPU in use across all nodes as a share o: CPU in use across all nodes as a share of allocatable CPU - the CPU Kubernetes can hand out to pods. Averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data).
CPU in use by the virtual machines in th: CPU in use by the virtual machines in this resource pool, in MHz or GHz, from its last report, however old.
CPU this container was using at its late: CPU this container was using at its latest reading, taken within the last 5 minutes. 100% is one full CPU core, so a container using several cores can show more than 100%.
CPU use of the busiest container on this: CPU use of the busiest container on this host in each interval of the selected range, which can be a different container from one interval to the next. 100% is one full CPU core.
CPU use of the host's busiest container,: CPU use of the host's busiest container, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). The busiest container is picked per interval, so it can change; 100% is one full CPU core.
CPU used by each task's container at the: Загрузка CPU контейнером каждой задачи по последнему измерению агента OneUptime (100% — это одно полное ядро CPU); показывается, только если измерению меньше 15 минут. Для задач на узлах, где агент не запущен, показывается N/A.
CPU used by this task's container at the: Загрузка CPU контейнером этой задачи по последнему измерению, отправленному агентом OneUptime (он снимает показания каждые 30 секунд); 100% — это одно полное ядро CPU. В отличие от списка задач, эта страница продолжает показывать это измерение, даже если ему больше 15 минут.
Capacity is the node's total CPU; alloca: Capacity is the node's total CPU; allocatable is what is left for pods after the operating system and Kubernetes take their reservation. Values are in cores, and an m suffix means thousandths of a core (500m is half a core).
Capacity is the node's total memory; all: Capacity is the node's total memory; allocatable is what pods can use after the system's reservation. Shown in Kubernetes units: Ki, Mi and Gi are kibibytes, mebibytes and gibibytes (1 Gi = 1,024 Mi).
Ceph's own health verdict from the clust: Ceph's own health verdict from the cluster's latest data: OK, Warning (WARN) when something needs attention, or Error (ERR) when data availability or safety is at risk. Unknown means no health data has arrived yet.

Cloud environments in this project - one: Cloud environments in this project - one per cloud platform, account and region - not counting archived ones. The line below breaks them down by provider.
Cluster CPU in use as a share of total a: Cluster CPU in use as a share of total allocatable CPU (what Kubernetes can hand out to pods) in each interval. Stays empty when the nodes do not report allocatable CPU.
Cluster CPU use across the whole selecte: Cluster CPU use across the whole selected range, as a share of all CPU cores on all nodes, with bigger nodes weighted more. 100% would mean every core on every node is busy.
Cluster cost over time, idle capacity in: Cluster cost over time, idle capacity included. Each point adds up the cost records that start in that interval of the chart, so longer ranges use bigger intervals and show taller points.
Clustered ESXi hosts that can run VMs, o: Clustered ESXi hosts that can run VMs, out of all hosts in clusters, from the latest inventory rather than the selected range. A host in maintenance mode or not responding is not effective, and standalone hosts are not counted.

Columns: {{columns}}. siteType must be o: Columns: {{columns}}. siteType must be one of this project's configured site types ({{siteTypes}}). parentName is optional for every type: leave it empty for a top-level site, or name any site that is not below this one in your site type hierarchy. Complete when the number of ready pods m: Complete when the number of ready pods matches the desired count and none are unavailable; In Progress otherwise, such as during a rollout or scale-up or while pods fail health checks. The bar shows ready pods out of desired.
Completed Go garbage-collection cycles i: Completed Go garbage-collection cycles in each interval. Worked out from the highest running counter when several instances report, so it is approximate; as a tile it shows the total for the selected range.

Connected while the Kubernetes agent kee: Connected while the Kubernetes agent keeps sending data to OneUptime; it switches to Disconnected about 15 to 20 minutes after data stops arriving. While disconnected, inventory counts on this page keep their last reported values.
Container memory (container.memory.usage: Container memory (container.memory.usage) in this environment for each interval. Every reading in an interval is added up, so a container that reports more than once per interval counts more than once - read it as a trend, not a total.
Containers on this host that reported CP: Containers on this host that reported CPU or memory in the last 5 minutes of the selected range. If none did (common on ranges over 12 hours), every container seen anywhere in the range is counted, including ones that have since stopped.
Containers whose recommendation (observe: Containers whose recommendation (observed demand plus 25% headroom) is more than 15% below their current CPU or memory request. Lowering those requests frees node capacity and saves money.
Containers whose recommendation is more: Containers whose recommendation is more than 15% above their CPU or memory request. They use more than they reserve, so a busy node can slow them down, and they are among the first killed or evicted when memory runs short.
Containers with cost data in the selecte: Containers with cost data in the selected range, including ones already right-sized. Each container of a workload counts once however many replicas it runs; idle capacity is left out.
Copies of the service running now, out o: Copies of the service running now, out of the copies it should be running - 2/3 means one is missing. A global service wants one copy on every eligible node.
Cost of all clusters over time, idle cap: Cost of all clusters over time, idle capacity included. Each point adds up the cost records that start in that interval of the chart, so longer ranges show taller points.
Cost of node capacity that no workload r: Cost of node capacity that no workload requested or used in the selected range (idle), plus cost the engine reports as unallocated. Running fewer or smaller nodes lowers it.
Cost of node capacity that no workload requested or used, across all clusters in the selected range. Unallocated cost is not included here.
Cost of the CPU this namespace was charg: Cost of the CPU this namespace was charged for in the selected range. The cost engine charges for the larger of what was requested and what was used.
Cost of the memory this namespace was ch: Cost of the memory this namespace was charged for in the selected range, based on the larger of requested and used memory.
Cost of the persistent volumes (disks th: Cost of the persistent volumes (disks that outlive a pod) this namespace used in the selected range.

Counts from the cluster's latest data, n: Counts from the cluster's latest data, not a time range: OSDs (the daemons that store data) that are up out of all OSDs, monitors in quorum out of all known monitors (only the monitor count when quorum is not reported), and pools.
Counts from the latest inventory the Kub: Counts from the latest inventory the Kubernetes agent sent: nodes, pods in any phase, namespaces, deployments, and containers defined in pod specs (init containers are not counted). They ignore the time range picker.
Coverage and instrumentation per service: Coverage and instrumentation per service in the selected time range

Credential sets tried against every host: Credential sets tried against every host in the range, in order, until one answers. Add one per group of devices that share a version and community or v3 user - mixed subnets are normal. Each extra config costs another SNMP timeout on every address that answers nothing, so keep the list to what the range actually contains.
Current CPU request and the recommended: Current CPU request and the recommended one: the 95th percentile of hourly CPU usage (95% of hourly readings were lower) plus 25% headroom. Needs 24 hours of data; within 15% counts as right-sized.
Current memory request and the recommend: Current memory request and the recommended one: the highest memory peak any replica reached, plus 25% headroom. Shows a dash when there is under 24 hours of data or no peak (the agent reads peaks from Prometheus).
Data read from and written to disk per s: Data read from and written to disk per second over the selected range, added up across every virtual machine and container in the cluster that reports disk counters.
Data received (In) and sent (Out) per se: Data received (In) and sent (Out) per second by all virtual machines and containers together over the selected range, worked out from the running byte counters Proxmox keeps for each guest.
Data stored in the pool, by Ceph's STORE: Data stored in the pool, by Ceph's STORED figure: what clients wrote, before replication copies. Shows a dash if the pool has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
Data stored in this pool, by Ceph's STOR: Data stored in this pool, by Ceph's STORED figure: what clients wrote, before replication copies. From the pool's latest report; a dash if that is older than 15 minutes.
Data this guest read from and wrote to i: Data this guest read from and wrote to its disks per second over the selected range, worked out from the running byte counters Proxmox keeps for it.
Data this guest received and sent per se: Data this guest received and sent per second over the selected range, worked out from the running byte counters Proxmox keeps for it.
Data this node read from and wrote to di: Data this node read from and wrote to disk per second over the selected range. Often empty, because Proxmox reports disk counters for virtual machines and containers rather than for nodes.
Data this node received and sent per sec: Data this node received and sent per second over the selected range. Often empty, because Proxmox reports network counters for virtual machines and containers rather than for nodes.
Datastore space this VM's files take up: Datastore space this VM's files take up now, against the total provisioned for it (used space plus what its disks may still grow into), with the share used, from the latest report.
Day boundaries and shift times on the ti: Границы дней и время смен на хронологии показаны в этом часовом поясе. Меняется только отображение — каждое расписание по-прежнему передаёт дежурство в своём часовом поясе.
Days until this datastore is full if it: Days until this datastore is full if it keeps growing at the rate seen over the last 24 hours, using a straight-line fit. Shown only when usage is growing and would fill within a year, or as Full now once it is full.
Deleting it removes it from: {{slos}}. A: Deleting it removes it from: {{slos}}. Any SLO left with no monitors stops being evaluated and shows as Misconfigured.
Deleting {{methodLabel}} removes {{count: Deleting {{methodLabel}} removes {{count}} notification rules and leaves {{cells}} with no rule.
Deleting {{methodLabel}} removes {{count}} notification rule and leaves {{cells}} with no rule.
Device counts for your six most common v: Device counts for your six most common vendors, as each device reported over SNMP. Devices with no vendor yet, such as ping-only ones, are grouped as Unknown, and each bar is relative to the largest vendor.
Devices assigned directly to this site,: Devices assigned directly to this site, not counting those in child sites. Up and down use each device's most recent check; devices still pending are in neither.
Devices in the project that are not assi: Devices in the project that are not assigned to any site, so they count toward no site's health. Selecting this tile opens them on the device list.
Devices marked offline, plus devices who: Devices marked offline, plus devices whose latest reading shows battery below 20% or signal weaker than -100 dBm. Battery and signal only count if the device reported in the last 15 minutes, and this list ignores the time range picker.
Devices online out of all devices, count: Devices online out of all devices, counted from the most recent data the fleet sent rather than from a time range. Shown in red when any of them is offline.

Devices online out of all devices, counted like the Online Devices tile from each device's latest up/down heartbeat in the selected time range. Until the heartbeats first load, or if none arrived in the range, it shows the counts from the fleet's most recent data.
Devices that sent an up/down heartbeat a: Devices that sent an up/down heartbeat at any time in the selected time range; a device that was silent for the whole range is not counted. If none arrived in the range, the count from the fleet's most recent data is shown.
Devices whose latest up/down heartbeat i: Devices whose latest up/down heartbeat in the selected time range says they are up, out of every device that sent a heartbeat in that range. If no heartbeats arrived in the range, the counts from the fleet's most recent data are shown.
Devices whose most recent check failed:: Devices whose most recent check failed: neither ping nor the SNMP walk answered, or a monitor-backed device's bound monitor reports it offline. Counts the whole project, whatever filters are set below.
Devices whose most recent check reached: Devices whose most recent check reached them: ping or the SNMP walk answered, or a monitor-backed device's bound monitor does not report it offline. Counts the whole project, whatever filters are set below.
Devices with no result yet: never polled: Devices with no result yet: never polled, no probe assigned, or monitor-backed with no monitor bound or reporting. Up, Down and Pending together add up to every device in the project.

Disk space this guest uses compared with: Disk space this guest uses compared with its disk size, at its latest report. For QEMU virtual machines Proxmox only sees the used space when the QEMU guest agent runs inside the VM; without it this shows 0 or N/A.
Disk space used on the OSD compared with: Disk space used on the OSD compared with its total size, with the share used in brackets. Shows a dash if the OSD has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
Disk space used on this OSD's device com: Disk space used on this OSD's device compared with its total size, from its latest report. Shows a dash if the OSD has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
Distinct platforms this app has been use: Distinct platforms this app has been used on so far, such as a browser's operating system or a mobile device model. Not limited to the selected range, and not a count of users or devices.

Read everything in the project. Change n: Читать всё в проекте. Ничего не менять.
Docker volumes on the node where the One: Docker volumes on the node where the OneUptime inventory poller runs, which is normally one manager. Volumes belong to individual nodes, so volumes on nodes without the poller are not counted.
Each bar is a function, and its width is: Each bar is a function, and its width is its share of everything profiled for this service in the time window picked beside it - CPU time by default, bytes for Memory, lock contention for Locks, and every type added together for Everything. The functions a bar calls sit below it.
Each child site's health, rolled up from: Each child site's health, rolled up from the devices at that site and at every site beneath it. No Data means nothing below it has reported yet.
Each marker is one {{siteType}} — click: Each marker is one {{siteType}} — click to open it.
Each row shows a person's full rotation: Каждая строка показывает полную смену человека; длительность учитывает только активные часы дежурства ({{restriction}}).
Each service's state at its newest sampl: Each service's state at its newest sample from the last 15 minutes: Running, Stopped, Paused, or a start, stop, pause or resume still in progress.
Each site's health, rolled up from the d: Each site's health, rolled up from the devices at that site and every site beneath it, leaving out child sites under maintenance: the worst device status unless its Settings set a share-of-devices-down rule. No Data means nothing below it has reported yet.
Each source is a metric + aggregation, g: Each source is a metric + aggregation, given an alias you can reference in the expression. Up to {{max}} sources.
Each unit's state at its newest sample f: Each unit's state at its newest sample from the last 15 minutes. Active means running, listening or waiting to fire; Failed means it crashed or exited with an error; Unknown means no state was reported.
Enabled ports with a working link / enab: Enabled ports with a working link / enabled ports with no link, from each device's last successful SNMP walk. Ports switched off by an administrator count in neither; No SNMP means the device is only pinged.
Enabled ports with no link, added up acr: Enabled ports with no link, added up across every device in the project from each one's last successful SNMP walk. It counts ports, not devices, so one switch with three dead ports adds three.
Environments currently marked as sending: Environments currently marked as sending telemetry. One switches to disconnected after about 15 to 20 minutes with no logs, metrics or traces, and back as soon as telemetry returns.
Environments not currently sending telem: Environments not currently sending telemetry: ones silent for about 15 minutes or more, and ones added by hand that have never reported. Check that the OpenTelemetry collector for each is running.
Errors and frustration signals in these: Errors and frustration signals in these sessions, added up. Errors: uncaught JavaScript errors, unhandled promise rejections and failed file loads; an error that keeps repeating adds at most one every 5 seconds. Frustration: rage, dead and error clicks and repeated reloads. A live session can show fewer until it is closed off.
Errors your app reported as exceptions i: Errors your app reported as exceptions in the selected range, such as uncaught JavaScript errors. The browser SDK does not send these on its own - they appear once your app records them (see Documentation).
Estimated monthly saving if every recomm: Estimated monthly saving if every recommendation below were applied, scaled from the selected range to a 730-hour month. Containers that would cost more after the change are not subtracted from it.
Events (spans) reported in each interval: Events (spans) reported in each interval, with the ones marked as errors as a second line. Page loads, requests and interactions all count.
Every OSD (a daemon that stores data, us: Every OSD (a daemon that stores data, usually one per disk) grouped by two flags: up means its daemon is running, and in means Ceph places data on it. Down + In is the risky case, because Ceph still expects data there but the OSD is not running.
Every interface found on this device in: Every interface found on this device in its last successful SNMP walk, including virtual ones such as VLANs and loopbacks, ports an administrator switched off, and muted interfaces.
Every network device in the project, spl: Every network device in the project, split by its most recent check: up, down, or pending when there is no result yet. Monitor-backed devices are judged by their bound monitor.
Every network site in the project at eve: Every network site in the project at every level of the hierarchy, from regions down to single units. Selecting this tile clears the filters on the list below.
Every span reported from this environmen: Every span reported from this environment (matched by its cloud platform, account and region) in the selected range, across all its services. One user request often produces several spans, so this is usually higher than the request count.
Every span this service reported in the: Every span this service reported in the selected range. A span is one timed operation - an incoming request, a database query or an outgoing call - and one request often produces several, so this is usually higher than the request count.
Every span your app reported in the sele: Every span your app reported in the selected range: page loads, the files and API requests they make, and clicks and other interactions. One page view usually produces several, so this is higher than the number of pages viewed.
Everything all Kubernetes clusters in th: Everything all Kubernetes clusters in this project cost in the selected range, as priced by each cluster's cost engine, including capacity no workload used.
Everything in the namespace's total that: Everything in the namespace's total that is not CPU, memory or storage, such as GPUs, network traffic, load balancers and shared costs.
Everything this cluster cost in the sele: Everything this cluster cost in the selected range, as priced by its cost engine: CPU, memory, GPUs, storage, network and load balancers, including capacity no workload used.
Everything this cluster cost in the selected range. The percentage and bar show its share of spend across all clusters.
Example: {{expression}} computes a perce: Example: {{expression}} computes a percentage from sources A and B.
Exceptions this service recorded in each: Exceptions this service recorded in each interval. Unhandled ones were marked as escaping the operation (span) that raised them; handled ones are the rest - usually caught by your code, or not marked either way by your SDK.
Exceptions thrown in .NET code in each i: Exceptions thrown in .NET code in each interval, including ones your code caught. Worked out from the highest running counter among instances and exception types, so it is approximate; as a tile it shows the total for the selected range.
Exceptions your app reported in each int: Exceptions your app reported in each interval of the selected range.
Fixes OneUptime AI proposed or applied o: Fixes OneUptime AI proposed or applied on this {{noun}}, newest first.
Flow export is not configured for this d: Flow export is not configured for this device, or nothing has arrived in the {{range}}. Point the device's NetFlow v5 export at your probe's IP on UDP port 2055 (and set PROBE_NETFLOW_RECEIVER_ENABLED=true on the probe).
For a service the status is its replica: For a service the status is its replica count: running tasks out of wanted tasks, the same figure as Replicas. It comes from the latest inventory snapshot.
For a stack the status only repeats its: For a stack the status only repeats its service count from the latest inventory snapshot; it is not a health check. The Services list shows whether each service has all its copies running.
Full page loads (documentLoad spans) in: Full page loads (documentLoad spans) in each interval of the selected range, with failed loads as a second line.
Full page loads in the selected range, c: Full page loads in the selected range, counted from the documentLoad span the OpenTelemetry browser SDK records each time a page is opened or reloaded. Route changes inside a single-page app are not page loads.
Goroutines (lightweight Go threads) aliv: Goroutines (lightweight Go threads) alive in the process; a count that keeps climbing and never drops usually points to a leak. Averaged across instances; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Green is 99.9% uptime or better, amber 9: Green is 99.9% uptime or better, amber 95% or better and red below that. A pale amber bar was entirely scheduled maintenance, and a hollow outline is a day before the site's first health rollup.
Groups of services deployed together, fo: Groups of services deployed together, for example with docker stack deploy, counted from the stack name Docker puts on each service. Services created on their own are not part of a stack.
Guest memory the VMs in this pool are ac: Guest memory the VMs in this pool are actively using, as estimated by ESXi, from its latest report. N/A when the pool has sent no data in the last 15 minutes.
Guests that at least one Proxmox backup: Guests that at least one Proxmox backup job includes, out of all guests; it checks job coverage, not whether recent backups succeeded. The bar is red while any guest is left out, and a dash means Proxmox has not reported backup information yet.
Here is a preview of who is on call and: Here is a preview of who is on call and when. Restriction windows are resolved in this schedule's timezone - {{timezone}}
Here is a preview of who is on call and when. This is based on your local timezone - {{timezone}}
Here is the final schedule of who is on: Here is the final schedule of who is on call and when. Restriction windows are resolved in this schedule's timezone - {{timezone}}
Here is the final schedule of who is on call and when. This is based on your local timezone - {{timezone}}
Hosts in the cluster that can run VMs, o: Hosts in the cluster that can run VMs, out of all its hosts, from its latest report. A host in maintenance mode or not responding counts toward the total but is not effective.
Hosts in this cluster that can run VMs (: Hosts in this cluster that can run VMs (effective), out of all its hosts, from the latest report. A host in maintenance mode or not responding is not effective and is flagged in red.
Hosts such as PCs, phones and printers f: Hosts such as PCs, phones and printers found in your switches' and routers' address tables (ARP and MAC forwarding tables) during SNMP walks. Every host found so far is counted, including ones not seen recently.
Hosts such as PCs, phones and printers t: Hosts such as PCs, phones and printers that devices assigned to this site found in their address tables (ARP and MAC forwarding tables). Every host found so far is counted, including ones not seen recently.
Hover one to see exactly where it sits.
Hover one to trace what it connects to.
How Windows starts the service: Automati: How Windows starts the service: Automatic (at boot), Manual (only when requested), Disabled (cannot be started), or Boot and System (loaded early, usually drivers).
How Windows starts this service, from it: How Windows starts this service, from its newest sample: Automatic (at boot), Manual (only when something asks for it), Disabled (cannot start), or Boot and System (loaded early in startup, usually drivers).
How busy each guest is, as a share of th: How busy each guest is, as a share of the CPU cores assigned to it, at its latest report. Shows N/A when the guest has sent no update in the last 15 minutes.
How busy each node's processors are, as: How busy each node's processors are, as a share of all its CPU cores, at its latest report. Shows N/A when the node has sent no update in the last 15 minutes.
How busy the cluster's processors are, a: How busy the cluster's processors are, as a share of all CPU cores on all nodes, so a big node counts more than a small one. It averages the last 5 minutes of the selected range, but often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours, and always when those 5 minutes have no data.
How busy the device's processor was at i: How busy the device's processor was at its most recent report, as a share of its full capacity. 100% means the CPU was completely busy.
How busy the port is: traffic in its bus: How busy the port is: traffic in its busier direction as a percentage of link speed, averaged between the last two SNMP walks, so short bursts in between are smoothed out.
How busy this guest was at its latest re: How busy this guest was at its latest report, as a share of the CPU cores assigned to it. It is the last value the agent sent, so it can be out of date if the agent has stopped reporting.
How busy this node's processors were at: How busy this node's processors were at its latest report, as a share of all its CPU cores. It is the last value the agent sent, so it can be out of date if the agent has stopped reporting.
How fast the containers on this host, al: How fast the containers on this host, all added together, received (In) and sent (Out) data over the network in each interval of the selected range, in bytes per second.
How fast this process read from and wrot: How fast this process read from and wrote to disk, in bytes per second, in each interval of the selected range. Worked out from the change in its running totals of bytes read and written.
How full the pool is: Stored divided by: How full the pool is: Stored divided by Stored plus Max Avail. It can reach 100% before the cluster's raw disks are full, because Max Avail is limited by the fullest OSD.
How full this pool is: Stored divided by: How full this pool is: Stored divided by Stored plus Max Available. Because Max Available is limited by the fullest OSD, a pool can reach 100% while the cluster still has raw space.
How full your fullest datastore is (used: How full your fullest datastore is (used space as a share of capacity) at its latest report, however old, named below; until the inventory loads, the fullest over the last 5 minutes of the range. Amber from 80%, red from 90%: the levels that mark the vCenter Degraded and Unhealthy.
How full your fullest storage volume is: How full your fullest storage volume is (used space divided by its size), from the latest report rather than the selected time range. It is the single fullest volume, not an average, and above 85% it marks the cluster Degraded.
How late the Node.js event loop ran sche: How late the Node.js event loop ran scheduled work; p99 means the 99th percentile: 99% of delays were shorter than this. Your SDK reports it per collection interval and those values are averaged across instances; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
How long ago OneUptime first saw this OS: How long ago OneUptime first saw this OSD in the data the Ceph agent sends, not how old the OSD or its disk is. It starts again from zero if the OSD was missing from that data for more than about 15 minutes.
How long ago this storage replication jo: How long ago this storage replication job last copied the guest's disks to the target node successfully. It turns amber after 1 hour and red after 6 hours without a successful sync.
How long each guest has been running sin: How long each guest has been running since it last started (its uptime). A stopped guest shows a dash.
How long each monitor's latest check too: How long each monitor's latest check took from each of your probes, such as a ping's round trip or a website's response time. Offline means that check failed, a dash means no result, and faded cells are over 10 minutes old. Global probes are not shown.
How long each node has been running sinc: How long each node has been running since it last booted (its uptime), not how long it has been part of the cluster.
How long full page loads took, from the: How long full page loads took, from the start of navigation to the browser's load event. p95 means the 95th percentile: 95% of page loads in the selected range were faster than this and the slowest 5% took longer. The median below is the typical load - half were faster.
How long the device had been running sin: How long the device had been running since it last started, as of its most recent report. The value does not keep counting while the device is silent.
How long the most recent run of this rep: How long the most recent run of this replication job took to copy the changes to the target node.
How long the probe's pings took to reach: How long the probe's pings took to reach this device and come back over the past hour, averaged per minute. Now is the latest minute with a reply, avg the mean of those minutes, and max the slowest minute rather than the slowest single ping.
How long this guest had been running sin: How long this guest had been running since it last started, as of its latest report.
How long this node had been running sinc: How long this node had been running since it last booted, as of its latest report.
How many NetFlow records this device exp: How many NetFlow records this device exported for flows that started in the selected range. Each record sums up one conversation (same addresses, protocol and ports) over a short stretch, so a long connection can produce many.
How many Proxmox nodes (physical servers: How many Proxmox nodes (physical servers) this cluster has, with any that are offline called out in red. Select the card to open the node list.
How many analysed sessions followed exac: How many analysed sessions followed exactly this journey from their first page to their last; the bar and percentage are their share of all analysed sessions. The 25 most common journeys are listed, and ones longer than 8 pages are compared on their first 8 and end in an ellipsis.
How many copies of the pod (replicas) th: How many copies of the pod (replicas) this deployment is set to run. An autoscaler, if one targets it, changes this number over time.
How many datacenters, clusters, ESXi hos: How many datacenters, clusters, ESXi hosts, VMs (powered on out of all, templates excluded) and datastores this vCenter has, from the latest inventory rather than the selected range. A kind with none is left out.
How many days back the calendar reaches: На сколько дней назад охватывает календарь (от 0 до {{max}}).
How many failed runs (Jobs) of this Cron: How many failed runs (Jobs) of this CronJob Kubernetes keeps, so you can look into them, before deleting the oldest. Kubernetes keeps 1 unless the CronJob sets another value.
How many finished, successful runs (Jobs: How many finished, successful runs (Jobs) of this CronJob Kubernetes keeps before deleting the oldest. Kubernetes keeps 3 unless the CronJob sets another value; 0 keeps none.
How many guests this cluster has - QEMU: How many guests this cluster has - QEMU virtual machines and LXC containers - whether they are running or stopped. Select the card to open the guest list.
How many main containers this pod runs,: How many main containers this pod runs, not counting init containers, which Kubernetes starts first to prepare the pod.
How many more pods this deployment needs: How many more pods this deployment needs to be fully available, such as pods still starting, failing health checks or waiting for a node. Shown only when above zero.
How many nodes and guests are in each Pr: How many nodes and guests are in each Proxmox high-availability (HA) state; HA restarts guests on another node when one fails. 'started' is normal, 'error' or 'fence' is a problem that marks the cluster Unhealthy, and 'migrate' or 'recovery' is temporary.
How many nodes should run this DaemonSet: How many nodes should run this DaemonSet's pod: every node its node selector, affinity and tolerations allow.
How many of the nodes that should run th: How many of the nodes that should run this DaemonSet's pod have one placed on them right now, even if it has not started yet.
How many of this deployment's pods are p: How many of this deployment's pods are passing their readiness checks, so Services can send them traffic.
How many placement groups, the chunks Ce: How many placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits pools into, the OSD holds; one with far more than its peers carries more data and load. Shows a dash if the OSD has not reported in the last 15 minutes.

How many placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits pools into, this OSD holds according to its latest report; more groups usually means more data and more load. Shows a dash if the OSD has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
How many pods must finish successfully f: How many pods must finish successfully for this job to be complete. 0 means no count was set, so the job is done once any pod succeeds and the rest have stopped.
How many pods the autoscaler last worked: How many pods the autoscaler last worked out its target should have, from its metrics and kept between the min and max. When this differs from the current count, scaling is under way.
How many pods the autoscaler's target ha: How many pods the autoscaler's target had when the autoscaler last checked it.
How many pods this StatefulSet is set to: How many pods this StatefulSet is set to run (its desired replicas), each with a stable name such as web-0 and web-1.
How many processes the host had, in any: Сколько процессов было на хосте в любом состоянии по последнему сохранению. Обновляется не чаще примерно раза в минуту.
How many services carry this stack's nam: How many services carry this stack's name, which Docker adds to every service a stack deploys. They count whatever their state, including ones scaled to 0; from the agent's latest inventory snapshot, taken every 5 minutes by default.
How many storage volumes Proxmox reports: How many storage volumes Proxmox reports, such as local disks, ZFS, NFS or Ceph, with storage shared by several nodes listed once per node. Select the card to open the storage list.
How many times Kubernetes has restarted: How many times Kubernetes has restarted this container in its pod. A count that keeps climbing usually means it is crashing or failing its liveness check.
How many times Kubernetes retries this j: How many times Kubernetes retries this job's failed pods before it gives up and marks the whole job as failed. Kubernetes uses 6 unless the job sets another value.
How many times Python's garbage collecto: How many times Python's garbage collector ran in each interval. Worked out from the highest running counter among generations and instances, so it is approximate; as a tile it shows the total for the selected range.
How many times a sample in the selected: How many times a sample in the selected range showed a different state from the one before it, such as Active to Failed. A failure and recovery that both happen between two samples is not seen.
How many times a status sample in the se: How many times a status sample in the selected range differed from the one before it, such as Running to Stopped. A stop and restart that both happen between two samples is not seen.
How many times the page was visited, cou: How many times the page was visited, counting returns after another page. A reload or two views in a row count once, and a return within the same recording chunk (about 15 seconds) is missed.
How much more data Ceph estimates can be: How much more data Ceph estimates can be written to the pool, allowing for its replication and for the fullest OSDs it uses.
How much more data Ceph estimates can st: How much more data Ceph estimates can still be written to this pool, allowing for replication and the fullest OSDs, from its latest report.
How much of the linked Ceph cluster's ra: How much of the linked Ceph cluster's raw disk capacity, across all of its OSDs (storage disks), is used, from its latest snapshot rather than the selected range. The bar turns amber from 75% and red from 90%.
How much of the machine's CPU the Java p: How much of the machine's CPU the Java process used, as the JVM reports it - 100% means every core was busy with this process. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
How much of the recording this person ac: How much of the recording this person actually played in this viewing. Paused time and jumps along the timeline do not count, and at 2x speed a minute of watching counts as two. Rounded down to 15-second steps, so less than that shows as < 15s.
How much of the requested CPU and memory: How much of the requested CPU and memory was actually used, averaged over the cost records in the range; above 100% means more was used than requested. Green from 70%, red below 40% - low values mean paying for unused requests.
How much of the time the Node.js event l: How much of the time the Node.js event loop was busy running code rather than waiting - near 100% the process is saturated and new requests queue. Averaged across instances; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
How much the round-trip time varied betw: How much the round-trip time varied between the pings in this test, measured as the standard deviation. High jitter can disrupt calls and video even when the average looks fine.
Idle spend as a share of total spend acr: Idle spend as a share of total spend across all clusters in the selected range. The bar turns amber at 25% and red at 40%.
Idle spend as a share of total spend in: Idle spend as a share of total spend in the selected range. The bar turns amber at 25% and red at 40% - a high share means paying for node capacity your workloads do not use.
If it is still unacknowledged, the whole: Если подтверждения так и нет, вся политика повторяется ещё не более {{times}}, а затем останавливается.
If no one acknowledges after the final e: If no one acknowledges after the final escalation level, this policy runs again from the top — up to {{times}} before it stops.
If still unacknowledged, the entire poli: Если по-прежнему нет подтверждения, вся политика повторяется {{times}}, а затем останавливается.
If the agent was uninstalled, or its key: If the agent was uninstalled, or its key or cluster name changed, run the install from the setup guide again with clusterName "{{clusterName}}".
If unacknowledged after {{duration}}, es: Если не подтверждено через {{duration}}, эскалация на следующий уровень
In job means at least one Proxmox backup: In job means at least one Proxmox backup job includes the guest, Not backed up means no job does, and a dash means no backup information has been reported yet. Whether recent backups succeeded is not checked.
In means Ceph is placing data on this OS: In means Ceph is placing data on this OSD. Out means it has been removed from data placement, by an admin or automatically after being down, and its data is served from other OSDs.
In means Ceph places data on this OSD. O: In means Ceph places data on this OSD. Out means it was taken out of data placement, by an admin or automatically after being down for a while, and its data lives on other OSDs.
In the last {{time}}, {{service}} spent: In the last {{time}}, {{service}} spent most of its {{category}} in {{function}} ({{share}} of the window).
In the last {{time}}, {{service}} spent most of its {{category}} in {{function}} ({{share}} of top sampled functions).
Inbound email is not configured. Please: Inbound email is not configured. Please ask your OneUptime administrator to set up the inbound email environment variables.
Inbound plus outbound packets per second: Inbound plus outbound packets per second that the port counted as errors between the last two SNMP walks. Anything above zero can point to a bad cable, a failing port or a duplex mismatch.
Incidents and alerts hidden: no access: Инциденты и оповещения скрыты: нет доступа
Incidents and alerts on this {{noun}} th: Incidents and alerts on this {{noun}} that OneUptime AI investigated, newest first.
Installed the {{collectorName}} with ins: Устанавливали {{collectorName}} с помощью install.sh? Запустите install.sh снова: теперь он запускает и этот агент — в контейнере {{service}}. При установке через Compose этот сервис уже есть в docker-compose.yml, с которым поставляется {{collectorName}}; если установка через Compose более старая, добавьте его в свой docker-compose.yml — все переменные ниже он возьмёт из того же .env.
Interaction to Next Paint for each route: Interaction to Next Paint for each route, averaged over the selected range, slowest first. In a single-page app this is the only place a slow view shows up on its own: the app-wide number mixes every route together. Routes come from the app.route (or url.template) attribute on web_vital.inp.
Interfaces that are enabled and have a w: Interfaces that are enabled and have a working link, as of the last successful SNMP walk. Muted interfaces are counted too.
Interfaces that are enabled but have no: Interfaces that are enabled but have no link as of the last successful SNMP walk, often an unplugged cable or a fault at the other end. Ports an administrator switched off are not counted.
Interfaces whose metrics are recorded an: Interfaces whose metrics are recorded and checked by monitors. Muted ones are still listed but not charted or alerted on, and this count can include interfaces the latest walk no longer reports.
It checks the whole chain — the agent, w: It checks the whole chain — the agent, what it scrapes, the {{resourceNoun}} name and the ingestion key — and says what is wrong.
It must still be \"{{functionName}}\". A: It must still be "{{functionName}}". A different name sends the data to a different function.
It must still be \"{{hostName}}\". A ren: It must still be "{{hostName}}". A renamed machine reports as a new host.
Last command error (last worked {{lastVe: Ошибка последней команды (в последний раз всё работало {{lastVerifiedAt}}): {{error}}
Latest apply and commit latency in milli: Latest apply and commit latency in milliseconds: how long this OSD takes to apply a write and to make it durable on disk, so high values mean slow writes for clients. Shows a dash if it has not reported in the last 15 minutes.
Latest: {{median}} ms median across {{co: Latest: {{median}} ms median across {{count}} probes ({{min}}–{{max}} ms)
Latest: {{median}} ms median across {{count}} probe ({{min}}–{{max}} ms)
Latest: {{median}} ms median across {{re: Latest: {{median}} ms median across {{responded}} of {{total}} probes ({{min}}–{{max}} ms)
Left divided by Sessions: the share of t: Left divided by Sessions: the share of the sessions that visited this page and ended on it. Sessions that saw only this page are included, and it is per session, not per visit.
Log records this service sent in each in: Log records this service sent in each interval, of every severity, with the Error and Fatal ones as a second line.
Log records your app sent in each interv: Log records your app sent in each interval, with Error and Fatal ones as a second line. Browser apps only send logs once the optional OpenTelemetry logs setup is added.
Logical CPU cores (each hyperthread coun: Logical CPU cores (each hyperthread counts as one) and total RAM, the sum of every memory state the collector reports; below, processes in any state. All three are the latest values saved on the host, updated at most about once a minute.
Look for OpenTelemetry export errors. A: Look for OpenTelemetry export errors. A 401 means the ingestion key was deleted or changed; a connection error means it cannot reach OneUptime.
Look for export errors. A 401 means the: Look for export errors. A 401 means the ingestion key was deleted or changed; a connection error means it cannot reach OneUptime.
Looks like the Microsoft Teams App Clien: Looks like the Microsoft Teams App Client ID is not set in the environment variables when you installed OneUptime. For more information, please check this guide to set up Microsoft Teams App properly:
Machines running Docker that have joined: Machines running Docker that have joined this swarm, from the agent's latest inventory snapshot (taken every 5 minutes by default). Ready counts the nodes the managers currently see as up; a node that is Down cannot run tasks.
Match alerts and start runbooks automati: Подбирайте оповещения и автоматически запускайте сценарии.
Match incidents and start runbooks autom: Подбирайте инциденты и автоматически запускайте сценарии.
Match scheduled maintenance events and s: Подбирайте плановые обслуживания и автоматически запускайте сценарии.
Matched by IP address · Last seen {{time: Matched by IP address · Last seen {{time}}
Matched by MAC address · Last seen {{tim: Matched by MAC address · Last seen {{time}}
Meant to be the jobs this CronJob starte: Meant to be the jobs this CronJob started that are still running. It is not read correctly from Kubernetes yet and shows 0 even during a run, so check the Jobs list for runs in progress.
Memory ESXi took back from this VM throu: Memory ESXi took back from this VM through the balloon driver in VMware Tools because the host was short of RAM. Only shown when above zero; it is a sign of host memory pressure.
Memory ESXi took back from this pool's V: Memory ESXi took back from this pool's VMs through the balloon driver, then memory it moved to disk swap, from the last report. Above zero means a host is short of RAM; swapping slows VMs badly.
Memory as a percent of each container's: Memory as a percent of each container's memory limit, or of the node's total memory when the service sets no limit. One line per container, averaged per interval.
Memory available to run VMs (effective): Memory available to run VMs (effective) against the cluster's total memory, from the latest report. Hosts in maintenance mode or not responding are left out of effective.
Memory each guest uses compared with the: Memory each guest uses compared with the memory assigned to it, at its latest report. Shows N/A when the guest has sent no update in the last 15 minutes.
Memory in use at the latest reading, as: Memory in use at the latest reading, as a percent of this container's memory limit. If the container has no memory limit, it is a percent of the host's total memory instead.
Memory in use on all nodes added togethe: Memory in use on all nodes added together in each interval, in bytes. Includes file cache the system can free when apps need the memory.

Memory in use on all nodes added together, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). It includes file cache the system can free, so it reads higher than what apps need.
Memory in use on all nodes together, as: Memory in use on all nodes together, as a share of their combined memory, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). The line below shows used and total memory at the latest data point.
Memory in use on each node compared with: Memory in use on each node compared with its total memory, at its latest report. Shows N/A when the node has sent no update in the last 15 minutes.
Memory in use on the Java heap, where yo: Memory in use on the Java heap, where your objects live. The JVM reports it per memory pool (such as Eden or Old Gen) and this is the average per pool and instance, not the total heap; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Memory in use on this node compared with: Memory in use on this node compared with its total memory, at its latest report.
Memory in use, added up across every tas: Memory in use, added up across every task or instance seen in the last 15 minutes from each one's latest reading. It is a live snapshot, so it ignores the selected time range.
Memory of this VM that ESXi moved to dis: Memory of this VM that ESXi moved to disk because the host ran out of RAM, shown only when above zero. Swapping slows the VM badly and marks the vCenter Unhealthy.
Memory the Go runtime is using apart fro: Memory the Go runtime is using apart from goroutine stacks - mostly the heap - or allocated heap bytes on older SDKs. Averaged across instances; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Memory the VM's operating system is acti: Memory the VM's operating system is actively using, as estimated by ESXi, against its configured memory, from its latest report. N/A when nothing arrived in the last 15 minutes.
Memory the VM's operating system is actively using, as estimated by ESXi, against the memory configured for the VM, with the share in use, from the latest report.
Memory the cluster can use to run VMs, o: Memory the cluster can use to run VMs, out of its total memory, from its latest report. Hosts in maintenance mode or not responding do not count toward the effective figure.
Memory the device was using compared wit: Memory the device was using compared with its total memory, both from its most recent report. A dash after the slash means the device does not report its total memory.
Memory this container was using at its l: Memory this container was using at its latest reading, taken within the last 5 minutes. File cache the system has not used recently, and can free on demand, is not counted.
Memory this guest is using compared with: Memory this guest is using compared with the most memory assigned to it, at its latest report.
Memory used by each container, not count: Memory used by each container, not counting file cache the system has not used recently. One line per container, averaged per interval.
Memory used by each task's container at: Memory used by each task's container at the agent's latest reading, not counting file cache the system has not used recently, shown only when that reading is under 15 minutes old. Tasks on nodes without the agent show N/A.
Memory used by the V8 JavaScript heap, a: Memory used by the V8 JavaScript heap, as the average per heap space (such as new and old space) and instance - not the total heap - or process physical memory when V8 heap metrics are missing. As a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Memory used by this task's container at: Memory used by this task's container at the agent's last reading, not counting file cache the system has not used recently. This page keeps showing that reading even when it is more than 15 minutes old.
Messages published and consumed on this: Messages published and consumed on this queue in each interval of the selected range, counted as the Published and Consumed tiles count them, with its spans of any kind that ended with an error. Only whole intervals are drawn, so the newest one, still filling, does not read as a drop.
Messages sent to Slack / Teams for this: Messages sent to Slack / Teams for this {{itemName}}.
Messages your instrumented applications: Messages your instrumented applications published to this queue in the selected range, from their producer spans: one per message, or per batch sent in one call. An application that records its sends only as client spans, as some AWS SDK instrumentations do, is counted from those. Publishers that are not instrumented are not counted.

Messages your instrumented applications took from this queue in the selected range, from their consumer spans: one per message processed, or per batch. Receives that returned nothing are left out; an SQS receive call counts only when it reports the messages it returned, once per batch. Receives recorded as client spans are not counted.

Monitors OneUptime recommends for this {: Monitors OneUptime recommends for this {{resourceName}}, based on the telemetry the agent already sends. Pick the ones you want, choose who gets paged, and create them in one step.
Monitors keep the cluster map and must a: Monitors keep the cluster map and must agree as a majority (a quorum) for the cluster to work. This shows monitors in quorum out of all known monitors, or only the monitor count when quorum is not reported.
Monitors show In Quorum when they agree: Monitors show In Quorum when they agree with the majority on the cluster map, and Out of Quorum when they do not. Other daemons show Reporting if seen in the last 15 minutes; any daemon silent for longer shows Stale.
Must be the name the {{collectorName}} r: Должно совпадать с именем, которое сообщает {{collectorName}}, чтобы агент обслуживал этот ресурс ({{noun}}).
Name set clear — the line joins it to it: Name set clear — the line joins it to its marker
Namespaces in the latest inventory. A na: Namespaces in the latest inventory. A namespace is a named group that keeps one team's or app's resources separate from the rest of the cluster.
Network sites in the project. Unhealthy: Network sites in the project. Unhealthy sites are those whose health, rolled up from the devices at and beneath them, is non-operational, such as Degraded or Offline; sites with no data yet are not counted as unhealthy.
New alerts and incidents from this monit: New alerts and incidents from this monitor are suppressed until the parents recover; monitoring and status updates continue.
New alerts and incidents from this monitor are suppressed until the parent recovers; monitoring and status updates continue.
No data has arrived from this {{resource: No data has arrived from this {{resourceNoun}} yet, which is why it shows as Disconnected. Set up the {{agentName}} — it takes a few minutes.
No instrumented application consumed fro: No instrumented application consumed from this queue in the selected range.
No instrumented application published to: No instrumented application published to this queue in the selected range.

No notification rules use {{methodLabel}: No notification rules use {{methodLabel}}, so deleting it does not change how you are paged.

No one is on this policy yet, so there i: No one is on this policy yet, so there is nobody to check. Add on-call schedules, teams or users on the {{tab}} tab and their readiness shows up here.
