No poll has been attempted in the last {: No poll has been attempted in the last {{minutes}} minutes, so this verdict may be out of date — check that this device's probe is online and keeping up with its fleet.
No profile data in the last {{time}} for: No profile data in the last {{time}} for {{service}}. Try a wider time window — or, if you haven't sent profiles yet, {{setUpLink}}.
No reminder was sent. {{reason}} Ask {{n: Напоминание не отправлено. {{reason}} Попросите {{name}} завершить настройку уведомлений в разделе «Настройки пользователя».
No rule - pages here fall back to a veri: Нет правила — оповещения здесь идут через подтверждённый метод
No series of this metric in the selected: No series of this metric in the selected range carries this queue's attributes, so a monitor would watch nothing. Widen the range and try again.
No users are assigned to any layer in th: Ни в одном слое этого расписания нет пользователей, поэтому никого никогда не оповестят, и каждое направленное сюда оповещение останется без ответа.
Nobody is ever on call in this schedule,: В этом расписании никогда никто не дежурит, поэтому каждое направленное сюда оповещение останется без ответа. Разверните слой ниже и добавьте хотя бы одного пользователя.
Nodes (physical servers) that Proxmox re: Nodes (physical servers) that Proxmox reports as online, out of all nodes in the cluster, from the latest report rather than the selected time range. The bar turns amber when a node is offline and red when half or more are offline.
Nodes (the machines that run your pods): Nodes (the machines that run your pods) in the latest inventory, not the selected range. Nodes whose Ready check is failing are called out as not ready - new pods are not placed on them.
Nodes acting as swarm managers: they kee: Nodes acting as swarm managers: they keep the swarm's state and decide which node runs each task, and they can run tasks too. Every other node is a worker.
Nodes in the swarm at the agent's latest: Nodes in the swarm at the agent's latest inventory snapshot (taken every 5 minutes by default), shown as ready out of total. Ready means the managers see the node as up; the figure turns red when any node is not ready.
Nodes online out of all nodes, guests ru: Nodes online out of all nodes, guests running out of all guests, and storage volumes (shared storage once per node), from the latest report rather than the selected time range.
Nodes where this DaemonSet's pod is runn: Nodes where this DaemonSet's pod is running and ready, out of the nodes that should run one.
Nodes whose Ready check is not passing -: Nodes whose Ready check is not passing - the node agent (kubelet) is unhealthy, cannot run pods or has stopped reporting - so no new pods are placed on them. Any such node marks the cluster Unhealthy.
Nodes whose pod for this DaemonSet has s: Nodes whose pod for this DaemonSet has stayed ready for at least its minimum ready time (minReadySeconds), out of the nodes that should run one.
Nodes whose pod for this DaemonSet is ru: Nodes whose pod for this DaemonSet is running and passing its readiness check, out of the nodes that should run one. Green when all are, amber when some are, red when none are.
None of this queue's spans in the select: None of this queue's spans in the selected range records a message being handled: no consumer spans, leaving out receives that returned nothing and SQS receive calls. The Traces tab lists the spans it has.
None of this queue's spans in the selected range records a publish: no producer spans, and no client spans that record a send. The Traces tab lists the spans it has.
Not configured — add SNMP credentials in: Not configured — add SNMP credentials in {{settings}} for interfaces and inventory

Примечание: в этом предпросмотре учтены только {{global}} пользовательские переопределения.
Nothing at this level matches “{{searchT: Nothing at this level matches “{{searchText}}”. The results under the search box look through your whole network, not just this level.
Nothing matching “{{searchText}}” at thi: Nothing matching “{{searchText}}” at this level is down, and no unit beneath it is either. Switch back to All to see everything here.
Nothing matching “{{searchText}}” at this level is down, and no unit beneath it is either. Switch back to All to see the map.
Nothing reports this device's health yet: Nothing reports this device's health yet — no monitor is bound to it.
Nothing under this site matches “{{searc: Nothing under this site matches “{{searchText}}”. Clear the search to see all of its children again.
Nudged apart — the line ends at the real: Nudged apart — the line ends at the real spot
Number of ESXi hosts (the physical serve: Number of ESXi hosts (the physical servers that run your VMs) in this vCenter, from the latest inventory, including standalone hosts that are not in a cluster.
Number of RADOS objects in the pool, the: Number of RADOS objects in the pool, the units Ceph stores data in. Large files and disk images are split into many objects, so this is not a count of your files.
Number of RADOS objects in this pool fro: Number of RADOS objects in this pool from its latest report. Ceph splits files and disk images into many objects, so this is not the number of your files.
Number of datastores, plus used space ag: Number of datastores, plus used space against total capacity added up across all of them. The bar turns amber at 80% and red at 90% of the combined capacity.
Number of monitor daemons, which keep th: Number of monitor daemons, which keep the master copy of the cluster map, from the cluster's latest data. This is a count only; open the cluster to see how many are in quorum.
Number of resource pools, which group VM: Number of resource pools, which group VMs so they can share and cap CPU and memory. Includes the built-in root pool that every cluster and standalone host has.
Number of vSphere clusters: groups of ES: Number of vSphere clusters: groups of ESXi hosts that pool their CPU and memory. Clustered hosts in maintenance mode or not responding are counted in red beside the number.
Number of vSphere datacenters in this vC: Number of vSphere datacenters in this vCenter, from the latest inventory. A datacenter is the top-level folder that holds hosts, clusters, VMs and datastores.
OSDs are the daemons that store data, us: OSDs are the daemons that store data, usually one per disk. Shows how many are running (up), how many Ceph places data on (in) and the total, from the cluster's latest data; amber when any are down or out.
OSDs are the daemons that store your dat: OSDs are the daemons that store your data, usually one per disk. This shows how many are running (up) out of all OSDs, and below it how many Ceph is placing data on (in), from the cluster's latest data.
OSDs that are running and holding data. This is the normal, healthy state.
OSDs that are running but excluded from: OSDs that are running but excluded from data placement, for example while being drained or removed. Ceph moves their data to other OSDs.
OSDs that are stopped and excluded from: OSDs that are stopped and excluded from data placement. Ceph has copied, or is still copying, their data to other OSDs.
OSDs that have stopped but are still exp: OSDs that have stopped but are still expected to hold data, so that data has fewer copies until they come back or Ceph marks them out and copies it elsewhere.
On-call duty rotates through {{people}},: Дежурство переходит по кругу между {{people}}, {{rotation}}. Каждый дежурит до следующей передачи, после чего дежурство переходит к следующему по порядку.
One marker per {{siteType}} at this leve: One marker per {{siteType}} at this level
OneUptime could not read the names of {{: OneUptime could not read the names of {{count}} group chats from Microsoft Teams just now, so they keep their current name (marked above). Click Refresh Chats again later; if it keeps happening, check the OneUptime server logs for Microsoft Graph errors.

OneUptime could not read the name of {{count}} group chat from Microsoft Teams just now, so it keeps its current name (marked above). Click Refresh Chats again later; if it keeps happening, check the OneUptime server logs for Microsoft Graph errors.

OneUptime last heard from this {{resourc: OneUptime last heard from this {{resourceNoun}} {{lastHeard}}. The {{agentName}} is no longer reporting — check on it with the steps below.
OneUptime matches the data by host.name,: OneUptime matches the data by host.name, which the collector reads from the machine's hostname. It has to be "{{hostName}}" (any letter case) for the data to land here. The host then switches to Connected within a few minutes.
Online nodes out of all nodes; Proxmox n: Online nodes out of all nodes; Proxmox needs more than half of its nodes online (quorum) to start guests, change settings or run high availability, so this turns red at half or fewer. It is worked out from which nodes report as online, not read from Proxmox's own quorum service.
Online or Offline, as Proxmox last repor: Online or Offline, as Proxmox last reported for each node. On Proxmox's built-in metric push, a node that stops sending data turns Offline about 2 minutes later while the other nodes keep reporting, and stays listed for up to 7 days.

Online or Offline, as Proxmox last reported for this node; on Proxmox's built-in metric push, a node that stops sending data turns Offline about 2 minutes later, reported by the nodes still sending. If the agent or the whole cluster stops sending data, this keeps showing the last known state.
Online or Offline, from each device's la: Online or Offline, from each device's latest up/down heartbeat. A dash means no heartbeat has arrived yet, and a registered device that stops reporting is eventually marked Offline.
Online or Offline, from the latest up/do: Online or Offline, from the latest up/down heartbeat this device sent. If it has stopped reporting, check Last Seen: a registered device that stays silent is eventually marked Offline.
Only data points where {{condition}} are: Only data points where {{condition}} are included in this source.
Only {{name}} can change their own notif: Изменить свои настройки уведомлений может только {{name}}, поэтому решение — напоминание с уже вставленной ссылкой.
Open Microsoft Teams and go to the group: Open Microsoft Teams and go to the group chat or one-on-one chat you want to notify.
OpenTelemetry exporter on your devices o: OpenTelemetry exporter on your devices or gateway
Optional: comma-separated {{targets}} fi: Необязательно: {{targets}}, доступные для исправлений, через запятую (* соответствует любой последовательности символов). Пусто — любые, кроме самого агента и его коллектора.
Optional: overrides the identity as the: Необязательно: переопределяет идентификатор как имя, под которым регистрируется агент.
Optional: overrides {{variable}} as the: Необязательно: переопределяет {{variable}} как имя, под которым регистрируется агент.
Other rules still cover this severity an: Other rules still cover this severity and rule type, so deleting this one does not leave a gap.
Outbound webhook requests sent for this: Outbound webhook requests sent for this {{itemName}}.
Overlaid queries use different units ({{: Overlaid queries use different units ({{units}}) — they share one axis, so values may not be directly comparable.
Pages visited just after this one, acros: Pages visited just after this one, across every analysed session that visited it, not only this step of the map. A session counts once per page, and the percentage is of all sessions that visited this page, so sessions that left from here add nothing. The 6 most common are listed.
Pages visited just before this one, acro: Pages visited just before this one, across every analysed session that visited it, not only this step of the map. A session counts once per page, and the percentage is of all sessions that visited this page, so landings add nothing. The 6 most common are listed.
People and teams responsible for this {{: People and teams responsible for this {{resourceName}}. They are notified about changes.
Physical memory (RAM) the .NET process o: Physical memory (RAM) the .NET process occupies, called its working set. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Physical memory (RAM) the process occupi: Physical memory (RAM) the process occupies, also called resident memory. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Physical memory (RAM) this process holds: Physical memory (RAM) this process holds, called resident set size or RSS, averaged over the last 5 minutes of the range (usually the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or with no recent data). The percentage below compares it with the host's total RAM.
Physical memory (RSS) held by this proce: Physical memory (RSS) held by this process in each interval of the selected range.
Physical memory (RSS) this process held: Physical memory (RSS) this process held at its newest reading in the last 15 minutes, with its share of the host's total RAM. The bar turns amber at 10% and red at 20% of RAM.
Placement groups (the chunks Ceph splits: Placement groups (the chunks Ceph splits each pool into) by state from the last 10 minutes: clean groups have every copy in place, degraded and undersized ones are missing copies, and Other is the rest, such as peering. A group can be in several states at once, so the segments are approximate.
Placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits: Placement groups, the chunks Ceph splits each pool into, that are degraded (missing copies) or undersized (on fewer OSDs than the pool's copy count), from the last 10 minutes of data. A group in both states is counted twice.
Pods by phase in the latest inventory: R: Pods by phase in the latest inventory: Running, Succeeded (all containers finished without error, such as completed jobs), Pending (not started yet) and Failed (stopped with an error). Not tied to the time range.
Pods in the latest inventory in any phas: Pods in the latest inventory in any phase - running, pending, completed or failed - not limited to the selected range. A pod is one or more containers that run together on a node.
Pods of this StatefulSet passing their r: Pods of this StatefulSet passing their readiness checks, out of the number it is set to run (its desired replicas).
Pods of this StatefulSet passing their readiness checks, out of the number it should run. Green when all are ready, amber when only some are, red when none are.
Pods of this deployment passing their re: Pods of this deployment passing their readiness checks, out of the number it is set to run (its desired replicas).
Pods of this job that are pending or run: Pods of this job that are pending or running right now, as of the latest snapshot from your cluster.
Pods of this job that ended in failure,: Pods of this job that ended in failure, counting every retry. Once failures go past the backoff limit, Kubernetes stops retrying and marks the job as failed.
Pods of this job that have finished succ: Pods of this job that have finished successfully. When the job sets a completions count, it is done once this reaches that count.
Pods placed on a node with at least one: Pods placed on a node with at least one container running, starting or restarting. Running does not mean healthy - a container can still be failing its readiness check.
Pods that have stayed ready for at least: Pods that have stayed ready for at least the deployment's minimum ready time (minReadySeconds, 0 unless set), so they count as available to serve.
Pods the cluster has accepted but not st: Pods the cluster has accepted but not started yet - usually waiting for a node with enough free CPU or memory, for an image to download, or for a volume. Any pending pod marks the cluster Degraded.
Pods whose containers have all stopped,: Pods whose containers have all stopped, with at least one ending in an error; they will not be restarted. Any failed pod, even one left behind by a finished job, marks the cluster Unhealthy.
Ports on this device from its last succe: Ports on this device from its last successful SNMP walk: up means enabled with a working link, down means enabled with no link. Ports an administrator switched off count in neither and fill the grey rest of the bar.
Ports that are enabled but have no link,: Ports that are enabled but have no link, summed over all devices from each device's last successful SNMP walk. A switch with three dead ports adds three to this number.
Post an update to your status page…: Post an update to your status page…
Powered on, Powered off or Template, inf: Powered on, Powered off or Template, inferred from whether the VM sent CPU data in the latest collection, so a suspended VM shows as Powered off. A dash means the VM has not been collected yet.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in the clu: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in the cluster, as counted by vCenter itself at its latest report.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this cl: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this cluster, as counted by vCenter itself at the latest report.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this vC: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs in this vCenter, templates excluded, from the latest inventory. Only the total is shown until the agent has reported power state.
Powered-on VMs out of all VMs, templates: Powered-on VMs out of all VMs, templates excluded, from the latest inventory; a VM that is off is not treated as a fault. Power state is inferred from which VMs send CPU data, so a suspended VM counts as off.
Processes and threads running inside all: Processes and threads running inside all containers on this host, added together and averaged over the last 5 minutes of the selected range (often the whole range on ranges over 12 hours or without recent data). Each thread counts as one.
Processes and threads running inside eac: Processes and threads running inside each container, averaged per interval. A count that keeps climbing can point to a leak or a runaway process.
Processes running or ready to run on a C: Processes running or ready to run on a CPU in the newest interval; the total on the line below counts every state and is updated at most about once a minute. Where states are not reported, as on Windows, it counts every process seen in the last 5 minutes.
Projected monthly change in cost if this: Projected monthly change in cost if this container's recommendation is applied, scaled from the selected range to a 730-hour month. Green is a saving; amber with + is the extra cost of giving it enough.
Proxmox does not report an uptime for st: Proxmox does not report an uptime for storage volumes, so this column normally shows a dash.
RAM in use across all ESXi hosts in each: RAM in use across all ESXi hosts in each interval of the selected range, as a share of their combined RAM.
RAM in use on each host against its tota: RAM in use on each host against its total RAM, with a bar for the share in use, from its latest report. N/A when the host has sent no data in the last 15 minutes.
Read and write operations per second (IO: Read and write operations per second (IOPS) from clients, added up across all pools. Worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running per-pool operation counters.
Read and write operations per second (IOPS) on this pool, worked out for each interval of the selected time range from Ceph's running operation counters.
Read-only: {{readExamples}}. An investig: Только чтение: {{readExamples}}. Расследование никогда не изменяет этот ресурс ({{noun}}).
Readiness for {{name}} was not checked -: Готовность {{name}} не проверялась: в этой политике больше получателей, чем охватила проверка, поэтому статус неизвестен, а не «готов». Полный список — на карточке «Готовность получателей».
Recorded sessions from this person that: Recorded sessions from this person that started in the selected range. The line below shows how many are still live (not yet closed off, which can take a few minutes after the visitor leaves), or else when their earliest session in the range started - not necessarily their first visit ever.
Recorded sessions that started in the pa: Recorded sessions that started in the past 24 hours; the server can reuse its answer for up to 30 seconds. Playable is every session except those closed with no footage or whose recording was lost, so sessions still recording count as playable. The newest start can be older than 24 hours.
Recorded time across these sessions, add: Recorded time across these sessions, added up. Each runs from its start to its last recorded moment, idle time included; one still recording counts what it has so far. The line below counts page changes made inside the app without a full reload; a page opened by a full load is not counted.
Refresh this page after a few minutes —: Refresh this page after a few minutes — the {{resourceNoun}} switches to Connected once its first data arrives.
Repeating is on, but the number of repea: Repeating is on, but the number of repeats is set to {{count}}, so the policy still runs only once. Set a repeat count to have it try again.
Replay upload bytes let through since 00: Replay upload bytes let through since 00:00 UTC for the whole project, all applications together, as the recorders sent them (usually compressed). The percentage is of this deployment's daily limit: amber from 80%, and at 100% recorders are told to stop until the next UTC day.
Replay upload bytes this application sen: Replay upload bytes this application sent since the 1st of the month (UTC), against its own monthly budget: amber from 80%, stopped at 100%. Only counted while a budget is set, so with none it reads 0, and bytes sent before a budget was set are not included.
Resident set size (RSS): the physical me: Resident set size (RSS): the physical memory (RAM) the Python process occupies. Averaged across instances in each interval; as a tile it shows the average over the selected range.
Round-trip time from the probe to this h: Round-trip time from the probe to this hop and back, from the first reply the hop sent. Routers often answer slowly, so one high hop matters less than a jump that carries on to the hops after it.
Route did not reach the destination.
